sources.title: Soda bread
sources.observation: The article explains that in soda bread, the lactic acid in buttermilk reacts with baking soda to form bubbles of carbon dioxide in the dough. It adds that such “quick breads” can be prepared quickly and reliably without the time and labor required for kneaded yeast breads.

sources.title: Bread, beer and wine: Yeast domestication in the Saccharomyces sensu stricto complex
sources.observation: The authors state that yeasts in the Saccharomyces sensu stricto complex ferment sugars into ethanol and CO2 and have been used for thousands of years to ferment bread, beer, and wine. They add that in Neolithic times, fermentations were probably initiated by naturally occurring yeasts rather than by consciously added cultures.
